content.title: How old is Rick Pitino? Age, career timeline for St. John's coach, from 1978 to 2026 | Sporting News
content.text: Rick Pitino is no stranger to the thrill of college basketball in March. Already a Naismith Basketball Hall of Famer, Pitino has led a record six NCAA teams to a March Madness appearance. With 37 seasons of collegiate head coaching experience under his belt, plus stints in the NBA and other basketball leagues, the latest program to benefit from the coach's years of wisdom is St. John's. The Red Storm recently secured their second NCAA Tournament bid in seven years, under Pitino. His first college head coaching job came in 1978. In 2026, Pitino is still going strong as one of the best leaders in the business.How old is Pitino, and how did he reach his current position at St. John's? The Sporting News has you covered on the details of the longtime coach's basketball career.MORE: Most March Madness wins ever, by coachHow old is Rick Pitino?Pitino was born on Sept. 18, 1952. He turned 73 years old in 2025 and will turn 74 before next college basketball season.Rick Pitino coaching career timelineLong before Pitino joined the Red Storm, he spent time with plenty of other prominent college basketball, NBA and even EuroLeague teams. Here's his full career timeline:1974-76: Hawaii assistant coach and interim head coachPitino's coaching career began as an assistant at the University of Hawaii. He went from a graduate assistant to a full-time assistant with the Rainbow Warriors, and when head coach Bruce O'Neil was fired during the 1975-76 season, Pitino stepped in as interim head coach.During Pitino's brief time leading Hawaii, it went 2-4 to finish the season.1976-78: Syracuse, assistant coachPitino was also an assistant at Syracuse in the start of his coaching career. He was hired under Jim Boeheim, who would wind up leading the Orange for decades before retiring in 2023.In his final tenure as an assistant at the collegiate level, Pitino helped Boeheim and the Orange reach the NCAA Tournament in 1977 and 1978.1978-83: Boston University, head coachBoston brought Pitino in as a head coach for the first time in 1978. The Terriers had struggled in recent seasons, going 17-34 in the two previous campaigns combined. Immediately, Pitino helped flip the script.Although Boston didn't make the NCAA Tournament until his final season with the team, 1982-83, it did have a winning record in all but one season under Pitino. MORE: Revisiting Rick Pitino's 2010 sex scandal at Louisville1983-85: New York Knicks, assistant coachIt wouldn't be his last stint in the NBA — or even with the Knicks — but Pitino joined New York as an assistant coach under Hubie Brown in 1983.The Knicks made the playoffs in 1983-84 led by Bernard King. However, they were one of the worst teams in the league the following season, and Pitino departed for his second college head coaching job. 1985-87: Providence, head coachPitino's fifth coaching job came in 1985 as he became the Friars' head coach. He would go on to make deep March Madness runs with plenty of teams, but Pitino's first Final Four came with Providence.Guard Billy Donovan, who later became a head coach himself, led the way as the Friars went 25-9 in 1986-87 and made a run through March. However, Providence fell to one of Pitino's previous employers, Syracuse, in the Final Four. Pitino made a jump back to the NBA soon after. 1987-89: New York Knicks, head coachPitino's first of two NBA head coaching roles with historic franchises began in 1987. The Knicks had won just 24 games in 1986-87, needing a new voice at the helm of their squad, and Pitino already had experience working for New York.The Knicks made the playoffs in both of Pitino's two seasons as head coach. In 1988, they fell to the Celtics in the first round. In 1989, Michael Jordan and the Bulls eliminated New York in the second round. 1989-97: Kentucky, head coachAfter yet another two-year coaching stint, Pitino finally stuck around in a role after joining Kentucky in 1989. The Wildcats had been dealing with the repercussions of a recruiting scandal under Eddie Sutton, needing a new coach to lead them back to an elite status. Pitino did just that, and in quick fashion. Kentucky missed the NCAA Tournament in Pitino's first two seasons, but then continued on to reach the following rounds of March Madness over the next four seasons, respectively: the Elite Eight, Final Four, second round, then Elite Eight.The Wildcats finally broke through with a title in 1996 after all of their deep runs through March in the 1990s. It was Pitino's first national championship, and it came with a win over Syracuse. Kentucky then returned to the title game in 1997 seeking to repeat, but fell to Arizona. Pitino left Kentucky after the championship loss. The following year, Kentucky won its second title in three years with Tubby Smith as head coach. MORE: How Rick Pitino's record compares to John Calipari's1997-2001: Boston Celtics, head coachAround eight years after he left the Knicks, Pitino was back with a storied NBA squad. The Celtics, who were still moving on from their successful Larry Bird-Kevin McHale era, hired Pitino in 1997. Unlike most of Pitino's basketball coaching jobs, his teams struggled in Boston. The Celtics missed the playoffs in each of his first three seasons as Pitino grew more frustrated. During the 2000-01 season, he stepped down as Boston's head coach. It was his final tenure in the NBA as he began focusing on college basketball once again. 2001-17: Louisville, head coachPitino is most well-known for his 16-year run at Louisville. He took over for another Hall of Famer, Denny Crum, as the Cardinals' coach in 2001, taking over a team that hadn't made the NCAA Tournament in two years after a long run of success under Crum. By Year 2 of the Pitino era, Louisville was back in the NCAA Tournament, and in 2005, he led the team to its first Final Four appearance in nearly 20 years. He became the first college head coach to lead three teams to a Final Four. In 2013, after years of making the bracket but no titles to show for it, the Cardinals came out on top. Pitino's team had reached the Final Four the season prior as well. At the time, he became the first Division I coach to ever lead two teams to national championships; however, all of Louisville's accomplishments from the 2011-12 to 2014-15 seasons have since been vacated by the NCAA.During the 2015-16 season, Louisville self-imposed a postseason ban during an ongoing NCAA investigation about an escort sex scandal involving recruits. Pitino's final season with the Cardinals came in 2016-17 after a winning record in all of his 16 seasons.In 2017, the NCAA charged Pitino for failure to monitor his program while it was involved in a sex-for-pay scandal. In 2018, the NCAA vacated Louisville's 2013 title 2012 Final Four appearance and a total of 123 wins and three losses.Pitino was placed on unpaid leave by Louisville after another recruiting scandal in 2017 that involved Adidas and recruits receiving pay. Pitino had a Louisville involving a lawsuit over his firing, but ultimately, it marked the end of a stint that included 13 NCAA Tournament appearances, with four not being counted in the record books. MORE: Rick Pitino coaching timeline2018-20: Panathinaikos, head coachPitino joined the EuroLeague in 2018, being hired by Panathinaikos, which is the basketball team of the Athens-based club Panathinaikos A.O.In his first season, Panathinaikos won the Greek Cup and Greek Basketball League's championship, but fell to Real Madrid in the EuroLeague playoffs. Pitino returned to the team in 2019-20, but the season was cut short by COVID-19. 2020-23: Iona, head coachPitino made his return to the college ranks in 2020 when Iona brought him on as its next head coach. The Gaels won just 12 games the season prior to hiring Pitino, but he turned the team around to make the 2021 NCAA Tournament thanks to a MAAC title. Iona won 25-plus games in each of the following two seasons under Pitino, making the tournament again in 2023 but falling in the first round. 2023-present: St. John's, head coachBeing hired by St. John's in 2023, Pitino has once again helped a college basketball team build a national presence with the Red Storm.St. John's increased its win total by two in Year 1 under Pitino, then became one of the best teams in the nation in 2024-25. This season, the Red Storm have ranked as high as No. 6 in the AP Poll and had 30 wins entering March Madness.After defeating Omaha in the first round of the NCAA Tournament, the Pitino-led Red Storm will be seeking to make a deep run as a No. 2 seed.MORE: Fewest points in a March Madness game
